title: How to Export Cortex XDR Logs
content_md: Use the XQL query APIs. Start a query with /public_api/v1/xql/start_xql_query, which returns an execution ID. Fetch the results with /public_api/v1/xql/get_query_results in JSON. That call returns up to 1,000 results inline; anything bigger comes back as a stream ID you pass to /public_api/v1/xql/get_query_results_stream. Authentication uses two headers: your API key in Authorization and its ID in x-xdr-auth-id. Cortex XDR collects detailed endpoint telemetry, plus network and identity data in many deployments. Prime Core has more than 24,000 unique detection rules, mapped to 676 MITRE ATT&CK techniques. Below is how to get data out, sanitize it, and investigate it for free in LogTotal. Get Started For Free Before you start An API key. Create one in the Cortex XDR settings (the standard key type is simplest) with a role that can run XQL queries. Note the key and its ID. Your API URL. It’s shown when you create the key, in the form https://api- .xdr. .paloaltonetworks.com. License and quota. The XQL APIs need a Cortex XDR Pro license. Queries draw on your XQL quota, and you can run up to four API queries in parallel. The dataset. Endpoint telemetry is in xdr_data, with fields such as agent_hostname, event_type, action_process_image_command_line and actor_process_image_name. Build the query in the Query Builder first. Export with the XQL APIs XDR="https://api- .xdr. .paloaltonetworks.com" H1="Authorization: $XDR_API_KEY" H2="x-xdr-auth-id: $XDR_API_KEY_ID" # 1. start the query
